title: Page availability
remediation: Check whether this page should be available, removed or private. Repair the route or server response if it does not match that intention.
verification: Fetch the same URL again. Check its response status and whether it contains the expected content.

title: Redirect history
remediation: Fix unintended redirect loops. Where several redirects occur, check that each one is needed and leads to the intended page.
verification: Follow every redirect again using the same crawl settings.

title: Indexing settings match your requirements
remediation: Make the page’s indexing instructions match the site owner’s requirements. Keep any deliberate exclusions.
verification: Fetch the page again and inspect its response headers, HTML and, when requested, browser results. This does not establish whether a search engine has indexed it.

title: JavaScript removes an initial noindex instruction
remediation: If the page should be indexed, send the correct indexing instruction in the initial HTML. Check whether the server and browser received equivalent content.
verification: Compare the initial HTML with the page after JavaScript runs. A browser check cannot establish whether Google has indexed the page.

title: Preferred-page declarations
remediation: Check that declarations of the preferred URL, known as canonical hints, agree with each other. A missing declaration does not always need a fix.
verification: Inspect the declarations in the initial HTML and after JavaScript runs. Confirm that they point to the intended preferred page.

title: Declared preferred page
remediation: Check whether the declared preferred page is available and has the intended indexing settings. Keep the source page’s evidence separate.
verification: Fetch the preferred URL separately and confirm that it is the intended destination.

title: Preferred URL matches your requirements
remediation: Set the approved preferred URL on the relevant page template.
verification: Check the source page and its declared preferred URL again.

title: Page title
remediation: Write a clear, accurate page title, or restore the title agreed with the site owner. There is no fixed character limit for this check.
verification: Read the actual title and ask an editor whether it describes the page usefully.

title: Required page content
remediation: Restore the content that the site owner expects visitors and crawlers to receive.
verification: Check for the required text again, using the same browser settings where applicable.

title: Page language matches your requirements
remediation: Serve the expected page language. Check whether language-specific routing sends visitors to the right page.
verification: Check the page again using the same language and screen-size settings.

title: Sitemap inclusion matches your requirements
remediation: Include or exclude the preferred URL in the sitemap according to the site owner’s requirements.
verification: Retrieve every configured sitemap again. If a sitemap is unavailable, its contents remain unknown.

title: Broken internal links
remediation: Check whether each linked page should exist, redirect elsewhere or remain removed. Update the links or destinations accordingly.
verification: Check the destination and the pages linking to it again.

title: Pages with identical main text
remediation: Review why the pages exist and which URL should be preferred. Identical text does not by itself justify merging pages.
verification: Compare the collected passages and the intended preferred URLs.

title: Structured-data JSON can be read
remediation: Fix invalid JSON in the structured data. Separately check that its types, properties and claims match the visible page.
verification: Parse the corrected JSON-LD and check the guidance for the search feature you intend to support.

title: Image text alternatives
remediation: Add alternative text that explains informative images. Keep empty alternative text for images that are purely decorative.
verification: Have a person review each image’s purpose, then check its alt attribute again.

title: Pages that may show an error message
remediation: Check whether the page is intended to show an error before changing its response status or content.
verification: Confirm that the content and response status match the intended error handling.

title: Language alternatives link back
remediation: Check that each language-specific destination links back to the corresponding alternatives.
verification: Fetch each declared language alternative again using the same crawl settings.

title: Pages without observed incoming links
remediation: Check whether important pages need more links from navigation or related content. Collect a fuller page inventory before treating a page as isolated.
verification: Crawl the relevant navigation and pages that should link to this page again.

title: Required page links
remediation: Restore the links that the site owner expects the page to provide. Preserve the intended visitor journey.
verification: Check the source page’s required links and fetch each destination again.

title: Required language alternatives
remediation: Restore the expected language labels and destination URLs.
verification: Check the declarations, links back from the alternatives and the destination languages.

title: Required structured-data types
remediation: Restore the expected structured-data types in the initial HTML or browser result, as configured. Include only factual information.
verification: Parse the data again and review the relevant Schema.org and search-engine guidance.

title: Basic fields for Google Product snippets
remediation: Check the Product name and the required offer, review or rating information. Make sure every claim matches the visible page.
verification: Check nested offer and review details, applicable policies and visible content separately. Passing this check does not guarantee a Google rich result.

title: Structured-data vocabulary and references
remediation: Review unrecognised type and property names for spelling mistakes or intentional extensions. Keep valid external references; do not invent missing entities or infer search-feature eligibility.
verification: Collect the page again under the same rendering requirements and inspect the versioned vocabulary review and reference states.

title: Selected Google structured-data fields
remediation: Correct required fields for the owner-selected Product or Local Business feature. Review Article recommendations only where they apply; do not invent dates, reviews or other facts.
verification: Collect the selected page again, inspect populated fields and unresolved references, then review the provider’s full policies separately. Field presence does not guarantee display.

title: Structured names and headlines in rendered page text
remediation: Review names and headlines missing from the browser text snapshot. Keep truthful wording and deliberate exclusions; inspect presentation manually before changing markup or page content.
verification: Collect a complete browser text snapshot and compare the declared selected names and headlines. Inspect other factual and visibility claims separately.

title: Declared product variants
remediation: Review group IDs, variant SKUs or GTINs and declared variation dimensions. Preserve valid off-page references and the owner’s single-page or multi-page design. Do not invent stock, prices or variant selection behavior.
verification: Collect the same declared group again and inspect its page-level IDs and dimensions. Check off-page variants and selection behavior separately before making a complete grouping claim.

title: Language-alternative declaration and destination review
remediation: Review self and return links, conflicting labels, full addresses, indexing settings and preferred URLs together. Preserve deliberate regional and fallback routing; do not invent translations.
verification: Collect every approved declared destination again under the same settings. Review unresolved destinations, supported codes, sitemap declarations and actual language routing separately.
